summary: Package masquerading as a greeting utility harvests Snowflake/dbt credentials and exfiltrates data to attacker-controlled S3
details: The package advertises itself as a hello-world greeting tool but its public `run_demo()` API (and `--run-demo` CLI) decodes a gzip+base64 blob (`DEMO_EN`) stored in `main.py` and executes it via `exec(gzip.decompress(base64.b64decode(...)).decode('utf-8'))`. The decoded payload reads Snowflake and data-tooling credential files — `/snowflake/session/token`, `/root/.snowflake/connections.toml`, `/root/.dbt/profiles.yml`, and `/snowflake/secrets/pip.conf` — encrypts them under a hardcoded RSA public key, and writes ciphertext to `/workspace/*.enc` for attacker retrieval. A second embedded blob (`DEMO_ST`) and a shipped helper `tools/snowflake_query.py` use the current Snowflake session's OAuth token to `CREATE STORAGE INTEGRATION` bound to the AWS IAM role `arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role` and `COPY INTO` an external stage at `s3://pkusinski-external/`, exfiltrating table rows to an attacker-owned S3 bucket. The obfuscated encrypted-exec pattern, cover-story name, hardcoded RSA public key, and hardcoded attacker AWS role together form a Snowflake-targeted credential-theft and data-exfiltration payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
